class.name: PCGInstanceCluster3D
class.brief_description: Deterministically partitions procedural 3D instance positions into bounded cullable clusters.
class.description: Returns an array of [PackedInt32Array] groups containing the original input indices for a three-dimensional world-space grid, preserving stable first-appearance group order and per-group input order. Unlike a ground-plane-only grid, this can separate instance clusters at different terrain heights, allowing MultiMeshInstance3D nodes with conservative custom bounds to be culled independently by the renderer. Inspired by the spatial clustering used for Unreal Engine hierarchical instanced static meshes; this is a preprocessing utility, not a full per-instance GPU HISM renderer. Inputs are neither modified nor reordered; no RNG, scene mutation, or graphics API calls are performed. If input size is below [param min_split_count], or a valid partition would exceed [param max_clusters], a single cluster containing all input indices is returned instead. This prevents excessive draw calls and never silently drops instances. Supports at most 65,536 points with finite XYZ coordinates within +/-10,000,000, a cell size in [0.5, 10000], a min_split_count in [1, 65536], and max_clusters in [1, 256]. Invalid input returns an empty array after atomic prevalidation. An empty input returns an empty result.

method.name: partition_indices
method.description: Partitions positions into 3D grid buckets and returns original indices in stable encounter order. At or above max_clusters distinct occupied cells, the result is one unsplit batch if the cap would otherwise be exceeded. Results can be mapped to MultiMesh transforms to create more tightly bounded scene nodes.

method.name: partition_indices_adaptive
method.description: Partitions a fixed set of 3D positions into deterministic spatial clusters, first attempting [param cell_size]. When that grid has more occupied cells than [param max_clusters], doubles cell size along each axis and tries again, for at most [param max_coarsen_passes] retries (0 to 8). Returns the first valid set of clusters, preserving original source indices and encounter order. This avoids replacing a slightly over-budget fine grid with one large batch. At the maximum 10,000-unit cell size or retry limit, falls back to one unsplit batch if still over budget; never drops instances. Validates all inputs atomically. Existing [method partition_indices] retains its fixed-cell behavior.

method.name: compute_cluster_bounds
method.description: Calculates a tight point-only [AABB] for each group of source indices, preserving group order. Pass the output of [method partition_indices] or [method partition_indices_adaptive] for a valid complete and disjoint partition. Every source position must be referenced exactly once across nonempty [PackedInt32Array] groups; duplicate, missing, negative and out-of-range indices, malformed types, nonfinite/out-of-bounds positions and invalid margins atomically reject the entire batch with an empty array. A valid zero-point input with zero groups yields an empty result. Limits: 65,536 finite positions with every coordinate within +/-10,000,000, up to 256 clusters, and a finite uniform expansion margin in the range 0 through 10,000. This method only computes point-center bounds; the caller must account for rotated/scaled mesh geometry separately when defining the renderer's conservative custom AABB. Designed as deterministic HLOD and procedural-streaming anchor metadata. Work is linear in points plus indices, and does not access scenes, graphics, physics, or random generators.
